request.spec:
On the sheet a transfer brought a person to, a steward can undo it on the same sheet-today they
arrived (a button on the row; any later day, anyone else, or a person who did not arrive by transfer
is refused with an error on the row): the person is transferred back to the sheet they came from by
exactly the transfer rules and lines, and this sheet then writes PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE name=<name>
to=<sheet id>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
On the sheet a transfer brought a person to, a steward can undo it on the same sheet-today they
arrived (a button on the row; any later day, anyone else, or a person who did not arrive by transfer
is refused with an error on the row): the person is transferred back to the sheet they came from by
exactly the transfer rules and lines, and this sheet then writes PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE name=<name>
to=<sheet id>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Undo transfer is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

**What it does:** each person row now has an "Undo transfer" button (`person-transfer-undo`). It sends the person back to the sheet they came from. Only a steward can do it, and only on the same sheet-today the person arrived. Anyone who isn't a steward, any later day, or a person who didn't arrive by transfer is refused with the row's error (`person-error`).

**How it works:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V94__person_arrived_on.sql`, adds an `arrived_on` date to each person. A transfer fills it in with the receiving sheet's today; if that sheet has no today set, it uses the real date.
- **Server:** a new `transfer-undo.POST.yml` endpoint. It first checks the undo is allowed (`CheckTransferUndo`), then runs the same steps as a normal transfer back to the original sheet, so the transfer rules apply too. The receiving sheet then writes `PERSON_TRANSFERRED … to=<origin>`, its rollup, `PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE … name=<name> to=<origin>` and the rollup again. The original sheet records the person's arrival as a normal transfer does.
- **Front end:** the button is in the new `PersonTransferUndo.tsx`, added to the transfer section of the row.

**Things to know:**
- **Second rollup line:** after `PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE`, the rollup is measured against the sheet's figures from before the undo. So it repeats the `TOTALS` line already written after the transfer line, which is what the test expects.
- **Merging on return:** if someone on the original sheet now has the person's name or alias, the person is merged into them on return, just as a normal transfer would. The test doesn't cover this.
- **Older transfers can't be undone:** people transferred before this change have no arrival date, so their transfers are refused.
